name: Ahmad
gender_note: A masculine given name; also used as a surname.
primary_meaning: Ahmad (Arabic أحمد, ʾAḥmad) is an Arabic male name from the root ḥ-m-d, “to praise”. It means “most praised” or “most praiseworthy” and is one of the best-known names of the Prophet Muhammad, which is why it is common across the Muslim world.
meaning_explanation: Ahmad comes from the verb ḥamida, “to thank, to praise”. It shares its root with Muhammad, Mahmud, Hamid and Hamad. In the Qur'an (61:6) Isa (Jesus) foretells a messenger named Ahmad, which most Muslim scholars understand as Muhammad.

etymology.morphology: Elative (afʿal) form of the root ḥ-m-d.
etymology.explanation: From the root ح م د (ḥ-m-d), verb ḥamida “to thank or to praise”.

origin.explanation: Arabic, spread with Islam. Its transliteration has one of the largest numbers of spelling variants of any name (Ahmed, Ahmet, Akhmad, Achmad…).

religion.association: Islamic — a name of the Prophet Muhammad
religion.explanation: In Surah al-Saff (61:6) Isa (Jesus) announces a messenger to come “whose name is Ahmad”; most Muslim scholars take this to mean Muhammad. Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari report Muhammad naming himself Ahmad. Some Western scholars, such as W. Montgomery Watt, argued that Ahmad was not used as a proper name for Muhammad until the second Islamic century.

quranic.note: Prophecy attributed to Isa of a messenger named Ahmad.

naming_context.context: Given in honour of the Prophet, often as the first element of compound names (Ahmad Ali, Ahmad Raza).
naming_context.interpretation: Chosen for its link with the Prophet and its meaning “most praised”.
naming_context.important_distinction: The meaning comes from Arabic grammar; its religious weight comes from the Qur'anic verse and the Prophet.

cultural.meaning: Some traditions regard Ahmad as the Prophet's more esoteric name; some Muslim scholars also compared it with the biblical “Paraclete”, a view that is not universal.

items: Ahmad is linked to the Qur'anic prophecy in 61:6.
Used as a personal name throughout Islamic history, e.g. Ahmad ibn Hanbal (founder of the Hanbali school).
history.person: The Prophet Muhammad, called Ahmad in Qur'an 61:6.

modern_usage: Common throughout the Muslim world; Ahmed is the usual Egyptian/English spelling and Ahmet the Turkish one.

urdu.name: احمد
urdu.meaning: سب سے زیادہ تعریف کیا گیا

pronunciation.note: Egyptian Arabic and Turkish say Ah-med / Ah-met.

variant_notes: Ahmed (Egypt, English), Ahmet (Turkish), Achmad (Indonesian), Akhmad (Central Asian/Russian transliteration).

faq.a: “Most praised” or “most praiseworthy”, from the Arabic root ḥ-m-d, “to praise”.

faq.q: Is Ahmad mentioned in the Qur'an?
faq.a: Yes. In Qur'an 61:6 Isa (Jesus) foretells a messenger “whose name is Ahmad”, understood by most Muslim scholars as Muhammad.

faq.q: Is Ahmad the same as Muhammad?
faq.a: They are different names from the same root, ḥ-m-d. Ahmad is considered one of the names of the Prophet Muhammad.

faq.q: Ahmad or Ahmed — which is correct?
faq.a: Both. They transliterate the same Arabic أحمد; Ahmed reflects Egyptian and Turkish pronunciation.
Muhammad, Mahmud, Hamid and Hamad all come from ḥ-m-d.

seo.title: Ahmad Name Meaning: “Most Praised” — Arabic Root, Qur'an 61:6
seo.meta_description: Ahmad (أحمد) is an Arabic boy's name meaning most praised, from the root ḥ-m-d. A name of the Prophet Muhammad in Qur'an 61:6. Variants Ahmed, Ahmet.

claims.claim: Ahmad is an Arabic male given name, one of the well-known names of the Prophet Muhammad.
It derives from the root ḥ-m-d, verb ḥamida, 'to thank or to praise'.
It is tied to the prophecy attributed to Isa in Qur'an 61:6.
It shares its root with Mahmud, Muhammad, Hamed and Hamad.
Hadith collections such as Sahih al-Bukhari report Muhammad calling himself Ahmad.
W. Montgomery Watt argued it was not used as a proper name for Muhammad until the second Islamic century.
Some scholars compared the name with the biblical Paraclete, a view that is not universal.
